newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLISH RELEGATION SCRAP GOES RIGHT TO THE WIRE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLISH RELEGATION SCRAP GOES RIGHT TO THE WIRE.

text.p: Four English premier league sides face an 11th-hour scrap against relegation on Sunday while Liverpool, Arsenal and Newcastle compete for a place in next season's European Cup.

One of the tightest relegation battles for several seasons is still raging, with Coventry, Middlesbrough, Sunderland and Southampton all under threat as they prepare for the final game of a long campaign.
Nottingam Forest are already relegated and two other sides will join them.
Coventry and F.A. Cup finalists Middlesbrough are favourites to go down and both face difficult away matches on Sunday knowing they must win to stand a chance of survival.
Middlesbrough travel to Leeds, who have not conceded a league goal at home this year.

Boro have already carved out away draws at Manchester United and Blackburn this week but another one at Leeds' Elland Road fortress will not be enough to save one of the most expensively-assembled sides in the league from an ignominious drop into the first division.
Even victory will not guarantee Middlesbrough safety -- their foreign heroes Juninho, Emerson and Fabrizio Ravanelli will have to rely on favourable results elsewhere if they are to stay up.
The same goes for Coventry, who visit Tottenham.
Coventry are the escape experts of the premier league, having survived in the lower reaches of the top flight on a limited budget for 30 years.
Like Middlesbrough, they have 38 points, two fewer than 17th-placed Sunderland and three fewer than Southampton.
But their influential player-manager Gordon Strachan is struggling to shake off an injury and this looks like the season they might finally go down.
Sunderland, who need a victory to ensure safety but could survive with a point, face a long trip south to Wimbledon -- not the easiest side to beat at the best of times.
Wimbledon ended Liverpool's outside title hopes with a 2-1 midweek victory and will push Sunderland right to the end of their tense season.
Southampton, who are almost certain to survive barring a complete disaster, travel to Aston Villa in the other tie affecting relegation.
At the top of the table, Liverpool travel to Sheffield Wednesday, Arsenal visit Derby and Newcastle entertain relegated Nottingham Forest.
With the league title already in Manchester United's hands, attention now centres on the fight for England's second European Cup berth for next season.
Victory would take Liverpool into Europe's premier competition alongside United. Arsenal and Newcastle need to win and hope their rivals slip up.
